gen_risks.description: Severe climate events such as floods, cyclones, and extreme heat waves could damage educational facilities and cause prolonged school closures, leading to learning loss.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate-resilient construction standards, elevated foundations, passive cooling design, solar panels, and utilize the Primary Learning Program (PLP) EdTech platform for remote learning continuity.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 12: Natural disasters caused by climate change, including floods, cyclones, and extreme heat, pose significant challenges for Cambodia, particularly affecting education.

gen_risks.description: Overloaded financial management staff at the Directorate General of Administration and Finance may delay processing transactions and submitting financial reports.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint additional qualified FM staff, including government officers and specialized consultants, within three months of project signing.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 63: The current FM staff at the Directorate General of Administration and Finance may be overloaded, potentially leading to delays in processing transactions.

gen_risks.description: Delayed approval of the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) could stall timely execution of project activities across multiple components.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and adopt a Financial Management Manual containing a simplified AWPB template and streamlined approval contents.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 63: The delayed approval of the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) may hinder the timely implementation of project activities.

gen_risks.description: School mentoring funding distributed to cluster lead primary schools may suffer from improper monitoring and local fiduciary leakage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Issue clear guidelines on School Mentoring Funding within the POM and deploy IT experts at each school cluster to oversee data and monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 63: There is a risk that school mentoring funding, which is to be spent at the schools, may not be properly monitored.

gen_risks.description: MoEYS procurement staff's limited knowledge of World Bank Procurement Regulations could lead to noncompliance and project execution delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign dedicated full-time government procurement officers to the project and provide targeted contract management training from World Bank experts.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 68: MoEYS staff’s limited knowledge and experience with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations, potentially resulting in project implementation delays and noncompliance.

gen_risks.description: Delays in receiving technical specifications and inputs from technical departments could bottleneck procurement packaging and bidding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Designate procurement focal persons within each technical department and define service-level standards in the Project Operations Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 68: possible delays in receiving technical inputs for procurement;

gen_risks.description: Governance risks, including potential corrupt practices in procurement activities, could undermine project integrity and cost-effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce mandatory publication of annual procurement plans and contract awards, and implement a robust procurement complaint handling mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 68: governance risks, including corrupt practices in procurement;

gen_risks.description: Inadequate ministry capacity for civil works contract supervision and management could result in construction delays and poor facility quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement procurement tracking forms, conduct specialized contract management training, and establish clear service standards for civil works supervision.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 68: inadequate capacity for contract supervision and management, which may result in implementation delays;

gen_risks.description: Administrative bottlenecks and delays in securing internal clearances from the Procurement Review Committee could slow contract awards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish formal service standards in the POM and grant sufficient delegation of authority to Bid and Procurement Review Committee members.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 68: possible delays in internal clearance from procurement review committee.

gen_risks.description: Transitioning Early Grade Learning (EGL) programs from donor-funded pilot projects to full nationwide implementation through government systems risks dilution of pedagogical fidelity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt an implementation science-informed learning agenda to rapidly test, evaluate, and adapt implementation features using real-time administrative data.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 35: Transitioning from successful, donor-funded interventions... to implementation at scale through government systems requires overcoming technical, financial, and capability constraints.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate primary teacher capacity and skills could impede the effective delivery of foundational literacy and numeracy curricula.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide structured teacher training packages, scripted lesson plans, and continuous peer-mentoring through funded cluster lead school mentors.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 9: insufficient teacher capacity to effectively fulfill their roles;

gen_risks.description: Weak human resource management systems hinder the equitable distribution, career progression, and continuous professional development of teachers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Modernize and digitize the Human Resource Management Information System (HRMIS) to automate HR business processes and teacher data tracking.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 9: poor human resources management, which impedes the efficient utilization of allocated resources.

gen_risks.description: Severe classroom overcrowding (over 50 students per class) reduces teacher-student interaction time and negatively affects learning outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Construct new climate-resilient classrooms prioritized specifically for primary schools exhibiting class sizes of 50 or more students.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 37: 76 percent of primary students learning in classes with more than 30 students. Analysis shows these large classes affect student learning.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate access to ECE and low parental awareness regarding early childcare may result in low readiness among Grade 1 entrants.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish 60 formal ECE classes, support community preschools, and run targeted communication campaigns on early childhood development.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 9: limited readiness among children to learn, resulted from inadequate access to quality childcare and early childhood education (ECE) services

gen_risks.description: Failure to achieve required technical quality and inter-ministerial alignment in Phase 1 of HRMIS development will prevent progression to Phase 2 system deployment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a joint working group between MoEYS and the Ministry of Civil Service early to ensure alignment with national civil service regulations.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 41: Progression to Phase 2 is conditional on Phase 1 results demonstrating quality and feasibility in terms of technical development and alignment.

gen_risks.description: Risks of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) during civil works or school activities could harm beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deliver GBV awareness training to teachers, implement enforceable codes of conduct for construction workers, and adapt the project SEA/SH Grievance Redress Mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 57: Tackling GBV remains a paramount concern in Cambodia... significant lack of comprehensive data on GBV prevalence...

gen_risks.description: Mismatch between the Early Learning Partnership Trust Fund closing date (April 2027) and the project closing date (December 2030) risks interrupting childcare funding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Frontload trust fund disbursements for early childcare infrastructure and capacity building prior to April 2027, transitioning ongoing costs to IDA financing.
gen_risks.evidence: Footnote 22: The closing date for the Trust Fund differs from that of the project. The Trust Fund is scheduled to close on April 30, 2027.

gen_risks.description: Scheduled phase-out of key development partner assistance by 2027 could leave gaps in early grade reading and math M&E and technical support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize project IDA credit resources to institutionalize EGL M&E frameworks within MoEYS central departments before donor exit.
gen_risks.evidence: Paragraph 46: On EGL, the main DPs have provided assistance... Their support is expected to phase out by 2027.

gt_risks.description: Environment and Social risk is rated Substantial due to (a) limited institutional capacity to manage environmental and social risks and impacts; (b) nationwide implementation of the project's activities; (c) possible exclusion of vulnerable groups (such as poor children, children with disabilities, and indigenous groups); and (d) other risks involving child protection, occupational health and safety, labor issues, and sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEA/SH).
gt_risks.mitigation: The project will develop a capacity-building plan for the Environmental and Social Safeguards Office and Project Management Unit, including hiring dedicated environmental and social specialists and providing targeted training. It will establish robust monitoring mechanisms to ensure support for vulnerable groups (universal design in new school/WASH construction, materials adapted for visually impaired students), strict adherence to worker codes of conduct, complaint redress and referral mechanisms, and construction site safety measures to protect school children and communities from labor influx and construction-related risks.
